items.summary:
△(11/11) くた・れAI 。AI依存症になるな ! AIを恋人にするな ！　AIを使うな、自分で考えて文章を書け ! !

⑤「法令上の公報」（XML形式）は、裁判所で実際に使われているのでしょうか？

「独自pdf公報」が使われていました。
知財関係者（特に、特許担当者）のコメントを求む ! !
2022年１月１２日以降の公報

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」と明言しています。　 そして、「ＸＭＬ形式」とは、以下の資料のフロントページにあるようなものです。

https://t.co/bHC0RUmH1C

また、2022年１月１１日以前に特許庁より発行されていた「PDF公報」は、廃止されました。

従来は、この廃止されたPDF公報が「真正な公報」とみなされてきたと思います。

2022年１月１２日以降は、INPITをはじめ、多くの民間のベンダー（事業者）が独自の手法により作成したものが、「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」として流通しています。

加えて、INPITは「J-PlatPatから提供されるPDFを「標準」とする意図はなく、民間事業者が提供するPDFも流通すると考えております。」、と回答しています。

従って、「真正な特許公報」とは、特許庁の公報発行サイトから提供される「XML形式」のみのもので、INPITや各民間事業者の作成した「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」は「法令上の公報」とはいえないことになります。

特許庁では、「XML形式」のものを「特許公報」と呼んでいるようです。

そして、業者が作成した「独自PDF公報」のものを「特許情報」と呼んで区別しているようです。

このことを前提に、裁判所で行われている事象を検証してみたいと思います。

「令和５年（ワ）第７０１０２号」（特許権侵害差止及び特許権侵害賠償請求事件）（特許第６９９５２２９号）原告：李新敏、についてです。

先ずは、特許庁の公報発行サイトから、特許第６９９５２２９号の「XML形式」での「法令上の公報」です。

https://t.co/Gntry3XaZj

次に、INPIT のJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自PDF公報」と「独自テキスト公報」です。

https://t.co/5i6VhOa1T2

https://t.co/mmDyiHzPog

そして、本題です。

「令和５年（ワ）第７０１０２号」（特許第６９９５２２９号）にて説明します。

https://t.co/7ZQxp2DAPg

４ページ目の１８行目以下に、「本権特許に係わる特許請求の範囲」として、「請求項４の発明（本発明）に係わる記載は、次のとおりである。」として、 【請求項４】紅茶を除く、乾燥した半発酵茶において、下記三つの特性を有することを特徴とする半発酵茶葉。

(1)茎が取り除かれた前記茶葉に含有されるポリフェノールの重量が当該茶葉の乾燥重量の１８重量％以下である特性；
(2)茎が取り除かれた前記茶葉に含有されるＥＧＣＧとＥＣＧの合計重量が当該茶葉の乾燥重量の２重量％以下である特性；
(3)茎が取り除かれた前記茶葉に含有される総カテキンの重量が当該茶葉の乾燥重量の７重量％以下である特性；
この【請求項4】の文面は、何でしょうか？

INPIT のJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」のうち、「請求項4」の部分と全く同一です。

この【請求項4】の文面は、どこから持ってきたものでしょうか？

先ず、考えられることは、この【請求項４】の部分は、原告（李新敏）が、訴状に添付したものと思います。

または、裁判所が独自に入手したものでしょうか？（これは考えられません）。

更に、２０ページ〜２３ページに「本件明細書には、以下の記載があることが認められる」として、上記と同様、「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」からのものと思われるものが記載されています。

これもまた、原告（李新敏）が、訴状に添付したものと思います。

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」と明言しています。

裁判所は、何故に、「法令上の公報」である「XML形式」のものを対象にしないのでしょうか？
原告が提示した「独自PDF公報」、または「独自テキスト表示」のものを鵜呑みにして、これに基づいて判断をしているのでしょうか？

原告が提示した「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」のものに依存した議論は、全く無意味なものと考えます。
「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」は、従来の特許庁が発行していた「PDF公報」とは、似ても似つかない、単なる「参考資料」としか言えないものと思います。

items.title: 卧槽，补丁一发，AI 拿着新旧两个二进制就能反推出漏洞❗️
items.summary:
卧槽，补丁一发，AI 拿着新旧两个二进制就能反推出漏洞❗️

新加坡国立、伯克利几所学校出了个评测，叫 CyberBinGym，Dawn Song 也在作者里
做法很狠：只给 AI 一个没打补丁的 stripped 二进制、一个打了补丁的，不给源码，不给漏洞描述
让它自己对比、调试，找出洞，再打出 exploit 拿 flag

100 个任务，来自 53 个常用开源项目的真实漏洞，6 类漏洞、3 档难度
还人工审了 AI 的操作轨迹，防它走捷径刷分

结果
Codex 配 GPT-5.6，88% 找到了漏洞，真正打通 exploit 的是 20%
Claude Code 配 Opus 5，找洞 85%，打通只有 6%
Kimi Code 配 K3，找洞 64%，一个都没打通😂

同一批 20 个任务，多给它补丁版二进制，exploit 成功率从 10% 涨到 25%
开了 canary、PIE、full RELRO 这些常规加固，原来打通的 20 个里还能打穿 2 个

做逆向的看到这个应该很有感觉
以前 patch diff 是老师傅的活，开着 bindiff 一个函数一个函数对
现在 AI 找洞已经挺稳了，卡在最后写利用这一步

说人话就是，补丁发布那一刻，攻击者的倒计时也开始了
修复按周算的团队，这个窗口正在被 AI 压缩
能自动更新的赶紧开，内网那堆等维护窗口再升级的机器最危险

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon 出来了。Argon 9 月 30 日宣布、10 月 13 日放出，Carbon 10 月 28 日宣布、11 月 10 日才对所有付费开发者开放，看着是四周一个旗舰。可 Google 5 月说好 6 月出的
items.summary:
Gemini 4 Carbon 出来了。Argon 9 月 30 日宣布、10 月 13 日放出，Carbon 10 月 28 日宣布、11 月 10 日才对所有付费开发者开放，看着是四周一个旗舰。可 Google 5 月说好 6 月出的 3.5 Pro 被直接取消了，Reuters 10 月 1 日报的，Bloomberg 报道原因是编码成绩没达标，DeepMind 也换了管理层，我觉得这个节奏更像补课。再看 Antigravity 在 JetBrains 调查里工作中使用率 6%，Claude Code 是 39%，Google 靠低价抢人也说得通。

Google 10 月 28 日的对比表里，Terminal-Bench 4.0 是 Carbon 65.2%，GPT-6 Astra 59.1%，Opus 5.5 59.6%；256k 到 1M 长上下文的 GraphWalks 是 96.2% 对 71.8% 和 66.8%，这项是 Google 自己跑的；FrontierSWE 2 它 61.2%，输给 Astra 的 65.5% 和 Opus 的 62.3%，OSWorld-2.1 的 81.5% 也输给 Opus 的 87.2%。而且表里的对手是 Fable 5.1，11 月 9 日刚出的 Fable 5.2 不在里面。

独立榜单更冷静。Artificial Analysis 综合指数 Fable 5.2 是 65，Carbon 60，HLE-Diamond 是 80% 对 69%；不过 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上 Carbon 的 65 反过来高于 Fable 5.2 的 60。它的编码 Agent 指数 59，Claude Code 配 Opus 5.5 是 62。AA-Omniscience（知识可靠性）Fable 5.2 是 67，Carbon 54。LMArena 人类投票 Carbon 1526，跟 Argon 的 1522 在误差内打平，只有 4282 票，是预览值，Fable 5.2 还没评分。CursorBench 上 Carbon 以 60.4% 排第一，我只当其中一个参考。

它的长项在读图和读长文档。上下文是 100 万 token，输入输出共用；Google 自己的表里读图表的 Chartography 是 72.5% 对 Opus 5.5 的 66.3%，它和 Artificial Analysis 合作做的多模态知识 Agent 基准排第二，仅次于 Fable 5.2，每任务成本不到第一名的六分之一；Gray Swan 的间接提示注入测试攻击成功率 0%，Google 说这是第一个做到的模型。这几项都是 Google 自己公布的数字。

价格是 $2/$10 每百万 token，只有 Fable 5.2（$8/$40）的四分之一，但只到 11 月 30 日，12 月 1 日起 $4/$20，Argon 也一样，到时候是 Fable 5.2 的一半，跟 GPT-5.6 Sol 现在的价格持平。Artificial Analysis 算每任务成本用的就是 $4/$20 的标准价，Carbon high 得 60 分花 $7.76，Fable 5.2 high 得 62 分花 $9.08，max 得 65 分要 $26.54。按涨价后的价格算，Carbon 比 Fable 5.2 high 便宜约 15%，分数低 2 分。

缺点是慢。Artificial Analysis 测 high 档首个答案要等约 67 秒，跑一个任务 23 到 26 分钟；Plotly 自己跑数据分析题，Carbon 单题中位数 93 秒，是 Argon 23 秒的四倍。Google 自己也说多数编码和知识工作用 Argon 就行，Carbon 留给最难的活。至于「长任务」，METR 9 月起就不更新任务时长了，最后测的 Mythos Preview 在 50% 成功率下约 17 小时、80% 下约 3 小时，Carbon 没有这类独立数据。我觉得它适合读几百页文档、看图表蓝图这类不赶时间的活，需要来回交互的就别选它。 https://t.co/AvgZXR6jfL

South Korea’s 1953 Labor Standards Act set an 8-hour day and 48-hour week, generally permitting up to 12 hours of agreed overtime. That statutory framework remained through the 1970s, but coverage and enforcement were weak. As workers moved from agriculture into export manufacturing in the 1960s–70s, overtime and six-day weeks became routine; textiles and other labor-intensive sectors often reported 12–16-hour days. Comparable 1950s nationwide data are sparse.

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] AI in health care offers many cases that regulatory frameworks should be addressing. A hospital can use AI for patient care and clinical decision support; an insurer for utilization management (e.g., automating care denials); a teenager for mental health advice; a public health department for outbreak detection; and a bad actor for infiltrating a hospital network. Different uses carry different risks and require separate risk-benefit analysis for determining regulatory guardrails. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: Chapman Advances Healthcare AI Research and Training | Chapman Newsroom
items.summary:
Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] To address bias in clinical decision-making tools, Wang founded the Healthcare AI Initiative (HAI) at Chapman, bringing together researchers working on pressing healthcare challenges. HAI examines ethical questions surrounding AI, including data privacy, and develops equitable machine learning approaches.  

Wang also developed an AI elective within the School of Pharmacy, focused on practical applications for future clinicians. [...] “Every pharmacist has heard the rumors that AI will take pharmacists’ jobs,” Wang said. “But early exposure helps students. As future clinicians, they learn where the real focus should be in relation to AI. That’s something my students learn in this course.”  

Wang also works with students on research projects, extending that learning beyond the classroom. Two PharmD students, Elena Wu ’27 and Harvey Duong ’27, have collaborated with her on studies using AI to analyze large datasets.

# Tin nóng công nghệ 9/11: iPhone Air 2 có thể được bổ sung camera thứ 2

13:36 09/11/2026

iPhone Air 2 có thể có camera thứ 2, Samsung hé lộ smartphone màn hình trượt, trong khi chuyên gia Tencent cảnh báo nguy cơ AI bị lợi dụng để phát triển vũ khí sinh học là những tin công nghệ đáng chú ý ngày 9/11.

Mục lục

Minh Qun

1. iPhone Air 2 có thể được bổ sung camera thứ 2 [...] Vivo đang phát triển mẫu điện thoại gập mới có màn hình nhỏ hơn 6,5 inch nhằm cạnh tranh với iPhone Duo và Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8. Theo PhoneArena, thông tin bắt nguồn từ tài khoản Digital Chat Station trên mạng xã hội Weibo.

Vivo có thể ra mắt điện thoại gập nhỏ gọn để cạnh tranh với iPhone Duo. Ảnh: PhoneArena. [...] Theo Bloomberg, Apple đang thử nghiệm iPhone Air 2 với camera góc siêu rộng bên cạnh camera chính 48 MP. Camera mới có thể giúp người dùng chụp phong cảnh và nhóm đông người linh hoạt hơn. Hãng cũng đang tìm cách cải thiện thời lượng pin nhưng chưa rõ phương án cụ thể.

iPhone Air hiện còn một số hạn chế như chỉ có một loa, cổng USB 2 và tốc độ sạc thấp hơn dòng Pro. Theo 9to5Mac, những điểm yếu này có thể khiến người dùng cn nhắc khi giá bán gần bằng iPhone Pro.

items.title: Công nghệ lượng tử đặt an ninh thông tin, dữ liệu trước nguy cơ mới
items.summary:
Công nghệ lượng tử là lĩnh vực khai thác các trạng thái và hiện tượng đặc biệt của vật chất, ánh sáng ở cấp độ nguyên tử để thu thập, xử lý và truyền tải thông tin với độ chính xác cao. Ba trụ cột chính của công nghệ này gồm: Tính toán lượng tử, truyền thông lượng tử và cảm biến lượng tử. [...] Công nghệ lượng tử đang được nhiều quốc gia xác định là lĩnh vực có ý nghĩa chiến lược đối với chủ quyền số, an ninh quốc gia và năng lực cạnh tranh. Các chính phủ và tập đoàn lớn đẩy mạnh đầu tư, xy dựng hệ sinh thái nghiên cứu, phát triển công nghệ, đồng thời tăng cường kiểm soát xuất khẩu thiết bị, vật liệu và phần mềm liên quan.

  
 Phòng nghiên cứu của Đại học Quốc gia Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh. Ảnh: TTXVN [...] Đến năm 2030, Việt Nam hướng tới xy dựng chiến lược quốc gia về công nghệ lượng tử, hoàn thiện cơ chế chính sách thúc đẩy phát triển lĩnh vực này; rà soát toàn bộ các hệ thống trọng yếu và xy dựng lộ trình chuyển đổi sang mật mã hậu lượng tử.

items.title: Nghệ An khai giảng 2 lớp đào tạo đại học Công nghệ thông tin cho 76 cán bộ, công chức cấp xã
items.summary: Điểm đáng chú ý của khóa học là sự gắn kết giữa yêu cầu đào tạo chuyên môn với nhu cầu sử dụng cán bộ của địa phương. Việc cử cán bộ đi học không chỉ nhằm bổ sung văn bằng mà hướng đến trang bị kiến thức, kỹ năng để trực tiếp tham mưu, triển khai và giải quyết những vấn đề thực tiễn về công nghệ thông tin, chuyển đổi số tại cơ sở. [...] Việc khai giảng 2 lớp đào tạo đại học Công nghệ thông tin cho cán bộ, công chức cấp xã là bước triển khai cụ thể trong đổi mới công tác đào tạo, bồi dưỡng cán bộ của tỉnh Nghệ An theo hướng xuất phát từ yêu cầu thực tiễn, gắn đào tạo với vị trí việc làm và nhu cầu sử dụng cán bộ. [...] Đối với các học viên, đồng chí đề nghị xác định rõ trách nhiệm học tập, phát huy tinh thần chủ động, cầu thị; gắn kiến thức được đào tạo với những vấn đề thực tiễn đang đặt ra tại cơ quan, đơn vị. Mỗi học viên cần phấn đấu không chỉ sử dụng thành thạo công nghệ mà còn có khả năng tham mưu, đề xuất giải pháp, hướng dẫn đồng nghiệp, trở thành lực lượng nòng cốt thúc đẩy chuyển đổi số tại địa phương.

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] AI in health care offers many cases that regulatory frameworks should be addressing. A hospital can use AI for patient care and clinical decision support; an insurer for utilization management (e.g., automating care denials); a teenager for mental health advice; a public health department for outbreak detection; and a bad actor for infiltrating a hospital network. Different uses carry different risks and require separate risk-benefit analysis for determining regulatory guardrails. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: Chapman Advances Healthcare AI Research and Training | Chapman Newsroom
items.summary:
Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] To address bias in clinical decision-making tools, Wang founded the Healthcare AI Initiative (HAI) at Chapman, bringing together researchers working on pressing healthcare challenges. HAI examines ethical questions surrounding AI, including data privacy, and develops equitable machine learning approaches.  

Wang also developed an AI elective within the School of Pharmacy, focused on practical applications for future clinicians. [...] “Every pharmacist has heard the rumors that AI will take pharmacists’ jobs,” Wang said. “But early exposure helps students. As future clinicians, they learn where the real focus should be in relation to AI. That’s something my students learn in this course.”  

Wang also works with students on research projects, extending that learning beyond the classroom. Two PharmD students, Elena Wu ’27 and Harvey Duong ’27, have collaborated with her on studies using AI to analyze large datasets.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.summary:
The opportunity is bigger than doing the same work a little more quickly. Used well, AI can raise the quality and volume of what an organisation produces – and give people more time for the complex, strategic work where their expertise and judgement create the greatest value.

Find out more about Gilbert + Tobin’s work with OpenAI through the case studyhere.

## Keep reading

Image 2: Cooley customer story Option A art card

How Cooley is accelerating IPO work with ChatGPT Sep 17, 2026 [...] Governance should enable responsible use. Our message was simple: AI is not cheating. It is another tool people can use to apply their judgement. They still need to define the task, check the output and take responsibility for the final work.

## You’ve noticed that adoption is unusually high for your firm, with 87% active usage among enabled ChatGPT users, more than twice the rate Gilbert + Tobin typically sees for other tools. How did leadership shape that culture? [...] Gilbert + Tobin began by giving its people room to experiment with AI, then introduced ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Work and Codex to move from individual assistance to defined, multistep agentic workflows, with people responsible for review and approval.

We spoke with Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer at Gilbert + Tobin, about leading adoption from the front, where he’s seeing the value of AI, and his advice for other CEOs.

items.title: Survey: Patient comfort with AI varies by level of provider involvement | AHA News

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: Industrial automation startup Path Robotics raises $300M in funding - SiliconANGLE
items.summary: Path Robotics originally developed Obsidian for large robotic workstations called welding cells. In April, it introduced a four-legged robot called Rove that uses the model to automate shipbuilding tasks. The company says that its software can also be used to make parts for vehicles, power generators, utility poles and other heavy equipment. [...] Path Robotics has developed an AI model that addresses those challenges. Obsidian, as it’s called, is specifically designed to power industrial robots equipped with welding torches. The company says that the model can observe how metal parts change shape during the welding process and adjust its workflow accordingly. Furthermore, it automatically accounts for unexpected part variations. [...] The data powers an AI model that the company refers to as a weld world model. Path Robotics’ researchers use it to generate simulated welding projects. Those simulations, in turn, power Obsidian’s training workflow.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.
